clue.text: Queen avoids cheap restaurants and old clubs of course

indicators.note: something that avoids is kept out, so the royal letters are taken away from the eateries

parts.note: brasseries are informal, inexpensive restaurants
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch shuns budget eateries, and old golf gear naturally comes into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' points to a golf course: a brassie was an old wooden club, roughly a 2-wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassie is an obsolete wooden golf club with a brass sole plate.

clue.text: Flog cheat in test, hauled up before his head

indicators.note: in a down entry, something hauled up is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a crib is a sheet of answers smuggled into an exam

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A schoolboy caught cheating in an exam is dragged before the headmaster to be beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hauled up' turns CRIB into BIRC, and 'his head' adds H.
explanation.definitionFit: To birch someone is to beat them with a bundle of twigs as punishment.

clue.text: Crafty sort heading off member of resistance group

indicators.note: with its heading taken off, the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a partisan is a guerrilla fighting an occupying force

explanation.surface: A cunning type slips away from a band of resistance fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' strips the P from PARTISAN; 'Crafty' means skilled in a craft, not sly.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker, someone who practises a craft.

clue.text: Just like Jack, first to start trouble at airport

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
Orly is one of the main airports serving Paris

explanation.surface: Someone named Jack is the first to cause a disturbance at the terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack (Jack Tar) is an old nickname for a sailor, so 'just like Jack' means in the manner of a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailorly means befitting a seaman, and Jack Tar is slang for a seaman.

clue.text: Old people included in writer's surveys

parts.note: ex- means former or old

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other, as something included in a group

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, the novelists; the possessive is part of the surface
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: An author's questionnaires take in elderly folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's' wants to be a possessive linking words; it is the novelist Amis, Kingsley or Martin, and 'included in' places the people inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Examinations are inspections or scrutinies, as surveys of a property are.

clue.text: One work penned by writer made into a film

indicators.note: something penned by an object is enclosed by it, as in a pen for animals

parts.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a writing instrument
I is the Roman numeral one
op. is the abbreviation for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A single piece written by an author is turned into a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' is not an author but a ballpoint, the brand BIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A biopic is a biographical motion picture.

clue.text: Animal inhabiting Antigua, naturally

indicators.note: the answer lives inside the run of letters, as an inhabitant lives in a place

explanation.surface: A creature native to the Caribbean island of Antigua.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across antIGUA NAturally.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical lizard.

clue.text: China leads state conference

indicators.note: the first piece leads, coming before the second

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang china (plate) means mate, a pal
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A Chinese delegation heads a national summit.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is rhyming slang for mate, so china = PAL; the capital C disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaver was originally a parley or talk between parties, especially traders and local people.

clue.text: I'm amazed fruit's available in Northants town

indicators.note: goods available in a shop are found inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: Corby is a town in Northamptonshire, an English county
a lime is a citrus fruit; the 's is part of the surface

explanation.surface: Someone expresses surprise that some produce can be bought in a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor blimey is a British exclamation of astonishment; Northants is Northamptonshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Cor blimey is a Cockney exclamation of surprise, a corruption of 'God blind me'.

clue.text: Playwright — good one on reflection: stick around

indicators.note: the cane is placed around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a rattan is a walking stick made of cane

indicators.note: something seen in a mirror on reflection appears backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dramatist reflects that a fine one has a cane about him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns G and I into IG, which 'around' places inside RATTAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan was an English dramatist, author of The Browning Version.

clue.text: Perhaps Scottish sportsman's hairstylist?

definitions.meaning: curling, sliding stones on ice, is a sport strongly associated with Scotland
a roller used to put curls into hair; the question mark admits it is a gadget, not a person

explanation.surface: A Scotsman who plays sport is also a hairdresser.
explanation.definitionFit: One who plays curling on ice, and a roller for putting waves into hair.

clue.text: French girl and mother protest over the Spanish occupying piece of land

indicators.note: in a down entry the first pieces sit over the rest

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: the article occupies the island, sitting inside it

parts.note: an isle is an island, a piece of land in water
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A young Frenchwoman and her mother demonstrate against Spaniards taking over an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' works because this is a down entry, so the first pieces sit above the rest; 'occupying' puts the Spanish article inside the island to give ISELLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mademoiselle is the French title for an unmarried young woman.

clue.text: Musician censored songs from Germany during audition

indicators.note: during an audition things are heard, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: banned lieder: lieder are German art songs, and banned means censored

explanation.surface: A performer has his German songs suppressed while trying out for a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during audition' looks like a stage tryout, but it means heard: BANNED LIEDER said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandleader is the musician who directs a band.

clue.text: Carrier taking cheese to various cafés

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: various arrangements of the word are possible, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A delivery driver takes cheese round assorted coffee shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' makes FCASE from the cafés; the accent on the e is ignored, as usual in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefcase is a flat case for carrying documents.

clue.text: It might be planned for end of term

definitions.text: It might be planned for end of term

parts.words: It might be planned for end of term
parts.note: a formal school dance is arranged to celebrate the close of the school year

explanation.definitionFit: A prom is a formal dance held at the end of the school year, especially in North America.

clue.text: Evil sort has lowered head, not surprisingly, in Canadian city

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved down a place, so the head of the word drops

parts.note: a demon is an evil spirit

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A wicked person bows his head, unsurprisingly, in a city in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lowered head' moves the D of DEMON down one place, giving EDMON; 'surprisingly' turns NOT into TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmonton is the capital of the province of Alberta.

clue.text: Dope working for government dept?

parts.note: in means working, as a machine that is on
FO is the Foreign Office, a UK government department

explanation.surface: A fool is employed by a ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests a fool or a drug but here means information, as in 'give me the dope'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for inside information, and info is short for information.

clue.text: FBI agents wearing suit? That can't be true

indicators.note: the agents are inside, as a body is inside clothes it is wearing

parts.note: to suit is to fit
G-men, government men, is slang for FBI agents

explanation.surface: Federal agents in business suits are met with disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' reads as clothing next to 'wearing', but it is the verb meaning fit, which goes round the agents.
explanation.definitionFit: A figment is something imagined, an unreal invention.

clue.text: Unskilled worker is assistant to officer in mess

indicators.note: being assistant to someone puts the officer's title first, as the owner in a possessive

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, a police officer
the contraction 's stands for is
an orderly is an attendant doing basic tasks in a hospital

explanation.surface: A menial worker serves as an aide to an officer in the mess hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The orderly is assistant to the DI, so it is the DI'S ORDERLY. 'mess' is not the officers' dining hall but a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorderly means untidy, in a state of confusion.

clue.text: Physicist was in charge of family enterprise, originally

parts.note: to run a business is to be in charge of it
kin are one's family

indicators.note: the original, first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A scientist used to head the family firm, at first.
explanation.walkthrough: William Rankine was a 19th-century Scottish engineer and physicist, remembered in the Rankine temperature scale.
explanation.definitionFit: William Rankine was a Scottish scientist known for work in thermodynamics.

clue.text: Except for middle part, Christmas cake is hot

indicators.note: the central letter of the cake's name is left out

parts.note: stollen is a German fruit loaf eaten at Christmas

explanation.surface: Apart from its centre, a festive cake is warm.
explanation.walkthrough: STOLLEN has seven letters, the fourth an L; drop it. 'hot' is slang for stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for goods that have been taken illegally and are easy to trace.

clue.text: Defend position in foreign trench so vigorously

indicators.note: the letters are shaken up vigorously into a new order

explanation.surface: Soldiers hold their ground in a trench abroad with great energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vigorously' rearranges FOREIGN TRENCH SO into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight one's corner is to argue hard for one's own position or interests.

clue.text: One's angry look upset all but daughter

indicators.note: all but a letter means everything except it
in a down entry upset means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a regard is a look or gaze

explanation.surface: An angry person's expression is disturbed by everyone except his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns REGARD into DRAGER; 'all but daughter' drops the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A rager is someone in a fury.

clue.text: Ancient treasure found near area round Egypt's capital

indicators.note: the precious metal goes round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: gold is treasure

indicators.note: a capital letter is the first one of the word

explanation.surface: Precious finds are unearthed in a region surrounding Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is not Cairo but the first letter, E, which 'round' places inside GOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Age-old means having existed for a very long time.

clue.text: Garments in half closed bag

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word is its first three letters

parts.note: one's bag, as in 'not my bag', is one's thing

explanation.surface: Clothes are in a half-zipped holdall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bag' is not a holdall but one's interest, as in 'it's not my thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing means items worn on the body, collectively.

clue.text: Texan wounded by bullet ultimately surviving

indicators.note: wounded means damaged, so the letters are knocked out of shape
ultimately means at the end, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A cowboy from Texas is shot but lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wounded' rearranges TEXAN into EXTAN, then T from the end of 'bullet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant means still in existence, not lost or destroyed.

clue.text: Possible source of meat, as a rule expensive, so we're told

indicators.note: what we are told is heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: reign means rule and dear means expensive

explanation.surface: A meat supplier says, as a rule, it costs a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: REIGN DEAR said aloud sounds like the answer; reindeer meat is eaten in Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: Reindeer is eaten as venison in northern Europe, so the animal can supply meat.
